correctness.rationale: The main theorem is proved for every positive multipartite profile and every named palette lambda>r. A first force implies saturation of all lambda colours. Disjoint final palettes across parts imply multicoloured parts must be fully seeded; two empty monochromatic parts forbid any initial force. Conversely, represented colours outside any unseeded monochromatic part force that part, completing in at most two synchronous rounds. Counting onto colourings of each part by Stirling numbers then counts every successful restriction without collisions after subtracting the full-seeded monomial. Minimum-seed formula optimizes the capacities n_i-1 of multicoloured fully seeded parts and a single unseeded target; the palette cutoff follows from maximum neighbourhood size. Direct exact-integer exhaustive verification matches all seeded-size coefficients on 17 graph/palette cases through six vertices and structural membership on four cases; no finite check is substituted for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest exact published family result for complete multipartite graphs restricts to the chromatic palette lambda=r, at which no part may have multiple colours; the second nearest gives only r=2,lambda=3. The new assertion treats the complementary lambda>r regime with a new multicoloured-part full-seeding obstruction and a Stirling-weighted classification for all part profiles, plus exact minimum seed count. Primary 2024 full-text inspection and targeted published-finding corpus/primary searches found no statement implying the claim. The 2026 initiating preprint was only abstract-accessible; its full text is a material originality risk, not asserted to have been checked.

value.rationale: The initiating literature presents a new and generally difficult graph polynomial. A complete exact family formula over all multipartite profiles and all palettes beyond the chromatic number fills a natural parameter gap left expressly out of prior exact chromatic-palette work. It reveals a structural transition: multicoloured parts must be entirely precoloured, but uncoloured monochromatic parts can be resolved in at most two rounds. The full coefficient enumerator and separately exact minimal forcing-domain expression are reusable combinatorial invariants; the K_{2,2,2},lambda=4 example produces 288 genuinely partial optimum assignments, not the already-known lambda=r formula. The result is not based merely on a numerical gain or rebranding a known scalar statistic.
